figures.before: What MEP Means and Why Coordination Matters
figures.alt: Commercial interior rough-in with coordinated HVAC ductwork, sprinkler mains, conduit racks, cable tray, piping, and support systems before drywall
figures.caption: Coordination determines whether the building systems can be installed, serviced, inspected, commissioned, and finished without the field discovering conflicts after the space is already constrained.

figures.before: MEP Submittal Review: What to Check Before Approval
figures.alt: Commercial restroom under construction with accessible clearances, wall backing, plumbing rough-ins, and metal-stud framing
figures.caption: Submittal review connects the selected equipment and materials to the actual space. It needs to confirm dimensions, utilities, supports, clearances, controls, finishes, access, and compatibility with the surrounding work.

figures.before: MEP Closeout: As-Built Drawings, O&M Manuals, and Warranties
figures.alt: Construction planning table with drawings, measuring tools, a blank clipboard, and coordination materials
figures.caption: Closeout turns installed systems into usable operational information: as-built records, manuals, startup and testing evidence, training, warranties, maintenance access, and the outstanding items that must be resolved before turnover.
